newsitem.title: UK: London pulp futures market starts trading Thursday.
newsitem.headline: London pulp futures market starts trading Thursday.

text.p: The PULPEX London pulp futures market starts trading at 2 p.m. (1300 GMT) on Thursday, the London Securities and Derivatives Exchange OMLX said.
"The start of PULPEX means that conditions for international pulp trading are set to be transformed," OMLX, which will run PULPEX, said in a statement.

PULPEX contracts will be physically delivered, each contract representing 24 tonnes of northern bleached softwood kraft (NBSK), OMLX said. This will ensure that "the futures prices reflect the underlying market thus securing a transparent global market price for pulp".

"Initially, futures and options on NBSK pulp will be traded on PULPEX. Eventually, though, trading will be extended to encompass other pulp and paper products," OMLX said. Initially PULPEX will be open between 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. London time.
"We think the market has huge potential to be a very successful futures market," Peter Dodds, market maker in pulp at Sucden, said.
Pulp was one of the most volatile markets, he said, making it a "wonderful" candidate for a futures contract.
But he did not expect big initial volume. "Futures markets do take time to get established," he said.
